## 1. The data

<!-- What did you receive? How many runs, over what ranges? What do the notes say? -->

```{r}
#| label: look
glimpse(r3_raw)
summary(r3_raw)
r3_raw |> filter(!is.na(notes)) |> select(run_id, yield_pct, purity_pct, notes)
```

```{r}
#| label: scatterplots
#| fig-height: 6
r3_raw |>
  select(run_id, yield_pct, temp_C, residence_min, stir_rpm, feed_water_ppm) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(run_id, yield_pct), names_to = "predictor", values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = value, y = yield_pct)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ predictor, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Yield (%)")
```

## 3. A model for the yield

<!-- Start from the chemistry: which terms should be there, and in what form?
     (Curvature? Interactions? Does stirring matter at this scale?)
     Then check the model and improve it. Center the temperature. -->

```{r}
#| label: yield-model
fit_yield <- lm(yield_pct ~ temp_C + residence_min + stir_rpm + catalyst + feed_water_ppm, data = r3)
summary(fit_yield)
```

### Diagnostics

<!-- Residuals against the fitted values and against every predictor, a Q-Q plot,
     residuals in run order, leverage and Cook's distance, VIFs.
     What do they tell you, and what did you change because of them? -->

```{r}
#| label: diagnostics
#| fig-height: 6
r3_check <- r3 |> mutate(resid = resid(fit_yield), fitted = fitted(fit_yield))
r3_check |>
  select(run_id, resid, fitted, temp_C, residence_min, stir_rpm, feed_water_ppm) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(run_id, resid), names_to = "against", values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = value, y = resid)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ against, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Residual")
```

### Comparing candidate models

```{r}
#| label: compare
#| eval: false
fit_a <- lm(yield_pct ~ ..., data = r3)
fit_b <- lm(yield_pct ~ ..., data = r3)
anova(fit_a, fit_b)
AIC(fit_a, fit_b)
```

## 4. A model for the purity

<!-- The customer's limit is 98.5%. Which conditions lower the purity? -->

```{r}
#| label: purity-model
#| eval: false
fit_purity <- lm(purity_pct ~ ..., data = r3)
summary(fit_purity)
```

## 5. Choosing the operating conditions

<!-- Search a grid of settings inside the range of the data. Keep only the settings where
     the purity is safely above 98.5% (for example, where the lower end of the purity's
     95% prediction interval is at least 98.5), and find the highest predicted yield. -->

```{r}
#| label: grid-search
#| eval: false
grid <- expand_grid(temp_C = seq(175, 200, by = 0.5),
                    residence_min = seq(30, 75, by = 1),
                    stir_rpm = ...,
                    catalyst = c("A", "B"),
                    feed_water_ppm = 205)
grid$yield <- predict(fit_yield, newdata = grid)
purity_pi <- predict(fit_purity, newdata = grid, interval = "prediction")
grid$purity_low <- purity_pi[, "lwr"]
grid |> filter(purity_low >= 98.5) |> slice_max(yield, n = 5)
```

## 6. How sure are we?

<!-- At the recommended settings: a confidence interval for the average batch's yield,
     and a prediction interval for a single batch. Which one is "the yield we can promise"?
     Catalyst B: is its advantage at least 2 points? Show the interval, and test it. -->

```{r}
#| label: uncertainty
#| eval: false
best <- tibble(temp_C = ..., residence_min = ..., stir_rpm = ..., catalyst = "B", feed_water_ppm = 205)
predict(fit_yield, newdata = best, interval = "confidence")
predict(fit_yield, newdata = best, interval = "prediction")
confint(fit_yield)
```
